# GitHub Actions dependency lockfile

`.github/workflows/actions.lock` pins the direct and transitive action dependencies
of this repository's workflows to verified commits. It is generated by the
[official GitHub CLI extension](https://github.com/github/gh-actions-lock).

## Update workflow dependencies

From an authenticated GitHub CLI session in the repository root:

```sh
gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock --pin v0.4.1
# If already installed, keep the extension on the version used by CI.
# After adding a workflow or editing a uses: reference:
gh actions-lock --no-narrow
gh actions-lock --verify
```

Review and commit the workflow changes and the generated lockfile together.
Do not edit `actions.lock` by hand. `--no-narrow` preserves the written version
references instead of selecting a matching full version tag.

To intentionally advance an existing floating tag or branch to its current commit:

```sh
gh actions-lock --relock --no-narrow
gh actions-lock --verify
```

Review these dependency updates before merging. Never accept moved or unreachable
pins automatically. For an offline coverage check, use `gh actions-lock --verify-local`;
it does not verify upstream provenance. The `Verify Actions lockfile` workflow
runs the full verification on pull requests and pushes to the default branch.

## Coverage limits

The lockfile does not pin remote reusable workflow calls (`jobs.<id>.uses`) or
container image digests. Local `./` actions that use remote dependencies require
explicit migration or other handling; do not silently ignore them. See the
[GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles).
